EDIT:  I see that this has been discussed before.  There doesn't seem to have been a consensus, and I'm in mid-game here and need to make a ruling, so I'm going to say that since you're being asked to discard "your hand" instead of some number of cards, you can discard a hand of 0 cards and not have to destroy any stuff.  And conversely, I'm going to rule that if you have no cards in play, you can destroy all 0 of them.  (Unlike during that previous discussion, I never even considered the idea that your character card could count as a card in play which you have to destroy.  If that were the case, the card would simply read "each player discards his hand" and there would be no element of choice.)

posts.cooked: How is Absolute Zero immune to damage exactly? Misplaced Memo only works on non-hero targets, if that is where you're getting it from.

posts.name: dypaca
posts.cooked:
16. First of all, Absolute Zero is a hero target.  He will never be the non-hero target with the lowest HP.

However you resolve each damage to each target separately.  As you resolve each one, you determine if Misplaced Memo applies to that target.  If no other non-hero targets are equal or lower, then they are immune.  If they are tied for the lowest, or become tied for the lowest you can change which target is considered the lowest each time you resolve damage.  Theoretically if all non-hero targets were tied, you could treat them each as immune whenever they are dealt damage.  (Thought typically you would choose to make your current target not immune, so then it will take damage and become the lowest until something else takes damage).

"Threat" to the president says non-character card because I brought it up in the playtester forum.  I didn't point out the rest of the cards in that set because it seemed like it was just cluttering up the cards when the intention was obvious.

posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked: Yes. Irreducible damage can not be reduced, but it can be prevented or redirected. So Legacy's Fortitude has no effect against Plague Rat's irreducible damage, but Danger Sense will still prevent damage from Falling Statuary. posts.name: dypaca
posts.cooked:
Yes it can.  In addition to all the effective prevention Nielzabub brought up, things which use the term 'prevent', like Fanatic's Undaunted and Expatriette's Flak Jacket, can prevent irreducible damage.

There is also an odd possibility with Bunker's Incapacitated ability which prevents the next 2 damage to one hero.  Personally, I treat this ability as 'reduce the next damage to a hero by 2', so I would treat it as wasted if that damage is irreducible.  However, before Enhanced Edition, Wraith's base power used the same 'prevent' wording as Bunkers ability, and the ruling there was that it could prevent irreducible if it was 2 or less, but was completely wasted otherwise.  Since Wraith was presumably reworded specifically to get away from weirdness like that, I assume Bunker was just overlooked, but you can make your own judgement.

It was clarified somewhere or other that the former interpretation is correct. In your example, though, I would have the Snowman chomp on the Dreamer, and then redirect the environmental damage to another hero using that rule on The Dreamer's card.

Dreamy can only redirect damage to the lowest HP hero (this is a big contributer to her being Diff 3 IMO; part of why Omnitron is diff 1 is that he only ever attacks the high-HP heroes, which not only are less likely to abruptly die as a result, but also keep changing so that the damage isn't concentrated on a single victim).  Had the Snowman targeted Dreamy in that case, it would have dealt her 2 cold damage, which would redirect to Bunker and then kill him, and then dealt Dreamy 2 melee damage which the next-lowest hero would have to take.  It was safer just to let the Snowman eat Bunker directly, so that his second damage wouldn't occur.
